reports.title: Resolved: SIM-swap attempt on my line
reports.description: Someone tried to port my number. Operator confirmed and blocked it after I reported here.

reports.title: Suspicious 'ANTIC' email requesting my ID scan

reports.title: WhatsApp job offer asking for a 'processing fee'
reports.description: A recruiter promised a remote job but asked for a 10,000 FCFA processing fee up front.

reports.title: Cloned Facebook Marketplace seller took deposit
reports.description: Paid a 15,000 FCFA deposit for a phone; the seller blocked me right after. Sharing the account number.

reports.title: Fake bank 'account locked' SMS with shortened link
reports.description: Received an SMS saying my account was locked and to click bit.ly/xxxx to restore it. I did not click.

reports.title: Fake MTN MoMo reversal call asking for PIN
reports.description: Caller claimed to be MTN support and requested my MoMo PIN to reverse a wrong transfer. I hung up and am reporting the number.

reports.title: Phishing SMS impersonating Express Union
reports.description: SMS with a shortened link asking me to 'verify' my account within 24 hours or lose funds. The site copies the Express Union login page.

reports.title: WhatsApp account takeover spreading scam links
reports.description: My colleague's WhatsApp was hijacked and is messaging contacts with fake investment links. Several people in Buea received it.

reports.title: AI voice clone of a bank manager requesting transfer
reports.description: Received a voice note that sounds exactly like our branch manager instructing an urgent supplier payment. The number is not his.

reports.title: Fake NGO job offers collecting ID documents
reports.description: A Facebook page posing as an NGO recruiter collects national ID scans and 'processing fees' from applicants in Bamenda.

reports.title: Coordinated false health rumour on social media
reports.description: Viral posts claim a vaccination campaign is harmful. Rejected as duplicate — already tracked under an existing case.

reports.title: Ransomware email targeting a Douala SME
reports.description: Invoice-themed email with a macro attachment. One workstation was encrypted before IT isolated the network.

reports.title: Grooming attempt via gaming chat targeting a minor
reports.description: An adult account befriended a 13-year-old on a gaming chat and asked to move to a private app. Screenshots preserved and reported.

reports.title: Suspicious USSD popup draining airtime
reports.description: A repeating USSD prompt subscribed me to a paid service without consent. Airtime deducted three times.

reports.title: Fake agent cash-in overcharge scam
reports.description: A street agent added hidden fees on a cash-in and refused a receipt. Operator confirmed the agent code is unregistered.

reports.title: Cloned university portal harvesting student logins
reports.description: A look-alike domain mirrors the university login page and captures matricule and password. Confirmed by two students.

reports.title: Email account breach after credential leak
reports.description: Login alerts from an unknown city. Password was reused from a service that suffered a breach last month.

reports.title: Deepfake video of official soliciting donations
reports.description: A convincing AI video imitates a public figure asking for MoMo donations to a personal number. Spreading on WhatsApp.

reports.title: Coordinated election misinformation network
reports.description: Dozens of new accounts post identical false claims about polling logistics, timed to peak in the evening.

reports.title: BEC invoice fraud against a cooperative
reports.description: Attacker impersonated a supplier and changed bank details on an invoice. Caught before the second payment.

reports.title: Stolen national ID used to open a MoMo account
reports.description: Someone opened an account with my CNI details. Rejected as a duplicate of an existing case already under investigation.

reports.title: Lost phone with unlocked banking apps
reports.description: Phone lost with banking apps still logged in. Reported so numbers could be flagged; accounts since secured.

reports.title: Smishing link posing as the tax office
reports.description: SMS claims a tax refund is pending and links to a form requesting bank and MoMo details. Classic smishing.

alerts.title: Credential-Stuffing Attempts on Student Portals

dailyChallenge.question: Someone calls claiming to be from MTN support and asks for your MoMo PIN to “reverse a wrong transfer.” What do you do?

options.text: Give the PIN so they can reverse it
Hang up, never share PIN, and report on VARNIS
Ask them to call back later
Send a screenshot of your balance

dailyChallenge.correctExplanation: MTN (and banks) never ask for your PIN by phone. Report scams immediately.
dailyChallenge.incorrectFeedback: Not quite. Never share your MoMo PIN.
dailyChallenge.incorrectExplanation: Correct answer highlighted. Try again tomorrow for streak XP.

lessons.title: Spotting Phishing Messages
lessons.summary: Recognise fake SMS and emails that imitate MTN, Orange, banks and government portals.

sections.heading: Why this matters
sections.body: Phishing is the #1 entry point for account takeover in Cameroon. Fake SMS and emails imitate MTN, Orange, banks and even government portals to steal your PIN, OTP or password.

sections.heading: How to spot it
sections.body: Watch for urgency ('your account closes in 2 hours'), look-alike domains (mtn-cm-secure.net), requests for your PIN/OTP, and links that don't match the visible text.

sections.heading: What to do
sections.body: Never tap the link. Contact the institution through its official app or number. Then report the message on VARNIS so ANTIC can map the active campaign.

quiz.q: A message asks for your MoMo PIN to 'unlock a bonus'. You should…
options: Ignore and report it on VARNIS
quiz.explanation: No legitimate service asks for your PIN. Report it.

lessons.title: Mobile Money Fraud Defense
lessons.summary: Defend against reversal scams, fake agents and 'customer care' calls.

sections.heading: Why this matters
sections.body: MoMo fraud drains real savings. Scammers pose as agents, 'customer care', or friends in trouble to get you to approve a transfer or reveal your PIN.

sections.heading: How to spot it
sections.body: Red flags: unsolicited calls about a 'wrong transfer', pressure to act fast, and 'confirmation' SMS from a normal number instead of the official short code.

sections.heading: What to do
sections.body: Hang up, dial the official short code yourself, and never share your PIN — MTN and Orange never ask for it. Report the number on VARNIS.

quiz.q: Someone says they sent you money 'by mistake' and asks you to send it back now. This is…
quiz.explanation: Reversal scams rely on urgency. Verify through the official short code first.

lessons.title: Passwords & Two-Step Verification
lessons.summary: Build strong, unique passphrases and turn on two-step verification everywhere.

sections.heading: Why this matters
sections.body: One reused password can hand over your email, MoMo, social media and work accounts in a single breach.

sections.heading: What to do
sections.body: Use a long, unique passphrase per important account, turn on two-step verification everywhere it's offered, and change passwords from a trusted device if you suspect compromise.

quiz.q: The single best upgrade to account security is…
quiz.explanation: Even if your password leaks, the attacker still needs the one-time code.

lessons.title: Social Engineering: The Human Exploit
lessons.summary: How attackers manipulate trust, urgency and authority — and how to slow down.

sections.heading: Why this matters
sections.body: Most attacks in Cameroon target people, not systems — a convincing message, a fake agent, an urgent request.

sections.heading: The four levers
sections.body: Attackers lean on authority ('I'm from the bank'), urgency, scarcity ('offer ends now') and familiarity (a spoofed friend's name). Naming the lever breaks the spell.

sections.heading: What to do
sections.body: Slow down, verify through official channels, and never act on pressure. When in doubt, report it on VARNIS.

quiz.q: An 'urgent' request that pressures you to act immediately is a sign of…
quiz.explanation: Urgency is engineered to stop you thinking. Slow down and verify.

lessons.title: Safe Browsing on Public Wi-Fi
lessons.summary: Stay safe on shared networks at cafés, campuses and transport hubs.

sections.heading: Why this matters
sections.body: On untrusted networks, others nearby may be able to intercept unencrypted traffic or set up look-alike hotspots.

sections.heading: What to do
sections.body: Avoid logging into sensitive accounts on public Wi-Fi, confirm the network name with staff, and prefer your mobile data or a trusted connection for banking and MoMo.

quiz.q: Public Wi-Fi is risky mainly because…
quiz.explanation: On untrusted networks, avoid sensitive logins or use a trusted connection.
